content: Shag tobacco, also known as rolling tobacco, refers to finely cut tobacco that is specifically designed for creating self-made cigarettes. This is typically achieved by manually rolling the tobacco into rolling paper or by injecting it into pre-made filter tubes. The tobacco used in shag comes in various cutting styles, with most blends incorporating a simple mixture of loose cut tobacco. However, other cutting styles such as crumble cake, ribbon cut, and flake are also utilized. Some shag blends even feature more exotic cuts that resemble those used in pipe tobacco. Cigarettes made from shag tobacco are commonly referred to as rolleys, roll-ups, or hand-rolled cigarettes. The flat bags in which shag tobacco is packaged are often called tobacco pouches. Different Shag Styles There are numerous shag blends and tobacco styles, each distinguished by the types of tobacco used, curing techniques, and cutting methods. In some cases, additives such as sugar, glycerol, and fruit flavors are incorporated into the blends, resulting in a product that is somewhat similar to the shisha tobacco commonly smoked in the Middle East. American Shag: This style typically consists of a mixture of flue-cured domestic and/or imported tobacco combined with air-cured Burley tobacco. Virginia or Light Blends: These blends are primarily composed of several types of flue-cured Virginia tobaccos. Smooth Blends: These blends add Georgia tobaccos to a base of light Virginia tobaccos, creating a smoother flavor profile. Halfzware: This is a combination of light and zware (dark) shag, representing a typical Dutch-style blend. Turkish Blends: These blends predominantly feature Turkish (Native American) tobaccos, such as Yenidje, Samsun, and Bafra. Zware Shag: Known as a Dutch-style power blend, zware shag primarily consists of fire-cured Kentucky tobacco, Latakia, and air-cured Paraguayan tobacco.
